_construction:
Build scripts/pcn_ground_truth.json from evidence, not from a run's say-so.

CONSTRUCTION, stated so it can be audited:

  An MPN enters ground truth only if it is VERBATIM PRESENT in the source PDF's
  text layer. That is an independent check — the string is on the page or it is
  not — and it is what separates a real extraction from a misread. 893 of the
  896 MPNs the 2026-09-23 run emitted pass it.

  The three that do not are handled explicitly, never silently:

  - SYTYD-122HP-1+ (PCN23-002) is a MISREAD of a crop clipped 47% through its
    glyphs. It is excluded, and the part it misreads, SYTX9-122HP-1+, is added
    by hand: it IS verbatim in the source, it is the documented eighteenth part,
    and no run has yet emitted it.
  - TYC's two composite cells hold two customer part numbers each in one string
    ("TYC1056344-1,\n9501815SP-1"). Their CONTENT is real — both halves are on
    the page — but their SHAPE is wrong.

    THEY WERE CARRIED GLUED UNTIL 2026-09-24, flagged `malformed`, so that TYC's
    total read as the documented 24. THAT WAS A DEFECT IN THIS FILE, not a
    labelling choice: a tier-1 cell holding two part-shaped strings joined by
    comma+newline IS TWO PARTS, and ground truth that says otherwise asserts a
    wrong fact about the notice. Each is now SPLIT, which made TYC's count 26 and the
    corpus denominator 898 AT THE TIME. Both numbers have since moved, and the
    split is not why: on 2026-10-29 a 'Customer Part Number' column was ruled
    never an affected part, and these two composite cells are in exactly that
    column. They are still two ids each -- that part of this paragraph stands,
    and it is a fact about CELLS vs PARTS that holds whatever role the column
    has -- but they are now two CUSTOMER ids each, carried in TYC's
    `customer_mpns` rather than in its `mpns`. TYC's count is 16; the
    denominator is 512. Note what the sentence above already said while the
    count was 26: 'two customer part numbers each'. The file named them
    correctly and scored them wrongly for five weeks. The `malformed` list for TYC is consequently
    empty.

    This was found by the harness itself: the 2026-09-24 run scored TYC
    exact=24 AND malf=2, a combination that can only mean the malformed strings
    were in ground truth. Until the extractor learns the same split rule, TYC
    will score 24 exact + 2 spurious + 4 missing, i.e. the corpus reads 893/898.
    That shortfall is REAL and must not be closed by re-gluing this file. Prior
    reports citing a denominator of 896 stand as written; see
    docs/pcn-roll-c460ac6-2026-09-24.md.

  Every resulting per-notice count is then checked against the counts in
  docs/pcn-corpus-validation-2026-09-21.md. A disagreement aborts.

_corpus.statement: TEN DOCUMENTS IS THE CORPUS, and it stays ten until more notices are ingested. This is an enumeration, not an estimate. It was 8 until 2026-10-10: on 2026-09-30 all six sandbox MinIO buckets were listed in full (4061 objects), every PDF under every sustainment prefix was fetched and hashed, and the result was 8 distinct document contents with no unseen notice sitting in the bucket -- enumerated in docs/pcn-corpus-widening-2026-09-30.md. The corpus therefore does not widen by looking harder; it widens when new notices are ingested, which is exactly how it reached 10. TI PCN#20210316000.1 and IDT/Renesas PDN OV-19-05 were ingested into sustainment/inbound/ on 2026-10-10, the sustainment_sensor fired on both unaided, and both produced manifests under the versioned artifact layout.
_corpus.why_it_is_here: This block exists so the denominator lives where the GATE READS IT rather than only in prose. pcn_corpus_run.check_ground_truth() asserts TARGETS against it at startup and aborts on a disagreement, and pcn_corpus_gate.py copies it into docs/corpus-gate/latest.json so a committed report states the corpus it was measured against. A denominator that only a human can check is a denominator that drifts.
_corpus.denominator_history_note: 522 -> 512 on 2026-10-29, and it is a RE-LABEL, not a loss of recall. A 'Customer Part Number' column was ruled never an affected part: it carries the customer's own alias for the row's affected part, in the customer's numbering. TYC-PCN-24-210412.pdf was the only notice scoring that column as affected -- 10 of its 26 -- so it becomes 16 affected plus a new `customer_mpns` list of 10, and the corpus denominator falls by exactly those 10. NOTHING WAS DROPPED FROM THE RECORD: all 10 strings are still enumerated in this file, under the field that says what they are. A score of 512 is therefore NOT comparable to a score of 522 by subtraction -- the 10 moved out of the numerator and the denominator together, so an extractor that was scoring 522/522 would score 512/512 and an extractor that missed all 10 would have scored 512/522 before and 512/512 after. Any report citing 522 keeps its denominator; cite a score with the denominator it was measured against. 896, 898, 924 and now 522 are the historical denominators.
_corpus.source_sha256_rekey_note: THE CORPUS IS KEYED BY SOURCE CONTENT HASH (sha256), not by filename. Re-keyed 2026-10-12. Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf and Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf are ONE document under two filenames: byte-identical, measured 2026-10-12 inside the sandbox doc-tools pod, both 181899 bytes, both sha256 af5bfad3f9344eb1dc942230a33cb61b58fb911b977da2063fffbecb5788074c (md5 abe083fe...). Exactly one filename, Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf, is SCORED; Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf is a DECLARED ALIAS -- listed in documents[] so a fire of either name is anchored to the declared bytes, asserted rather than double-scored, and absent from notices{} and from TARGETS. Until this re-key that document was scored twice at 402 parts, which is why the harness reported 924 ground-truth parts over 522 distinct ones: 402 of the 924, 77% of the distinct corpus, was one document counted twice. gt_parts == distinct_parts == 522 now holds BY ASSERTION (pcn_corpus_run.check_ground_truth aborts the run if it ever stops holding), so a divergence means a new duplicate document entered the corpus or a part number is shared across two notices, and both need a ruling before a score is quoted. 896, 898 and 924 are HISTORICAL denominators: reports predating 2026-10-12 keep theirs, and a score must always be cited with its denominator. The superseded note said "Keep the duplicate pair -- it is how the two-ingest case is exercised". That was wrong: scoring one document twice does not exercise two ingests, it inflates one document to 77% of the corpus. The two-ingest case is now exercised by the declared alias plus the per-fire declared-bytes check (pcn_corpus_gate.check_declared_bytes). The removed notices{} entry for the alias was identical to the Rev1_EOL entry in count (402), mpns (same 402, set-equal), malformed and headers (both empty); it differed only in manifest and source. Its manifest key, preserved here so the second ingest is not lost from the record, was: sustainment/inbound/generated/Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN_pdf/manifest.json. Four S3 keys hold these bytes (see inbound_copies on the document entry).

documents.inbound_copies_note: Corrected 3 -> 4 on 2026-10-12 from a measurement, not a tune: four S3 keys hold these bytes -- sustainment/inbound/Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf, sustainment/inbound/diodes_2683/Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf, sustainment/inbound/diodes_bbox/Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf, sustainment/inbound/diodes_tier1/Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf. The declared 3 counted only the Rev1_EOL prefixes and missed the root FULLGREEN copy.

_corpus.widens_when: A new notice is ingested into processing-artifacts/sustainment/inbound/**. Then: add its TARGETS row, add its part numbers to notices{} under the same verbatim-presence rule as every other entry, and raise scored_entries / distinct_documents / gt_parts / distinct_parts here. Re-enumerating the bucket does NOT widen it -- that was done, and found nothing new.

TYC-PCN-24-210412.pdf.customer_mpns_source: The 'Customer Part Number' column of page 1's 17x8 grid: 8 non-empty CELLS holding 10 part numbers, two of the cells carrying two ids each joined by comma+newline ('TYC1056344-1,\n9501815SP-1' and '160303P1,\n160303P001'). Measured 2026-10-29 in the sandbox pod against the source PDF, pdfplumber default 'lines' strategy, grid #5 of page 1: the 'Part Number' column yields exactly the 16 `mpns` above and this column yields exactly these 10, character for character. THE ROW-LEVEL PAIRING IS NOT ASSERTED HERE -- the measurement enumerated each column, not which affected row each customer id sits against -- and the ruling scores customer_mpn as its own column, so the set is what this file claims. A future pass that measures the pairing should add it rather than assume it.
TYC-PCN-24-210412.pdf.source: 16 from the 'Part Number' column. RE-LABELLED 2026-10-29 from count=26: the 10 values of the 'Customer Part Number' column moved to `customer_mpns` above. Ruled that a customer part number is NEVER an affected part -- it is the customer's own alias for the row's affected part, in the customer's numbering, not the manufacturer's. The previous reading was conflating two different things and asserting that TE Connectivity discontinued 10 part numbers that are not TE part numbers at all. docs/pcn-corpus-validation-2026-09-21.md s1 called both columns affected and that is now superseded; it was recorded there as an open question, not as a finding. The earlier 24 -> 26 correction (2026-09-24, the two composite cells carried glued) stands as a fact about CELLS vs PARTS and is unaffected by which column they belong to -- see _construction.

headers._note: HEADER ground truth, added 2026-09-30. Established from the page, not from a run: every value below is read off the source PDF's page 1, and the competing value each run produced is named so a future reader can tell a defect from a disagreement. TYC is the degraded-text-layer notice -- its layer drops the 'ti' ligature everywhere -- so for this notice the text layer is a KNOWN-DAMAGED source and may not settle a field by itself. Every field in this block is now established; there are no pending fields left here. (The `pending` status itself is NOT retired -- it is the mechanism that keeps an unestablished field out of both the pass and the fail column, and the next notice to get a headers block will need it.)

mfr.source: Page 1, centred heading directly under the TE logo: 'TE Connectivity'.

accepted._rule: ACCEPTED-VERBATIM SET, ruled 2026-10-09. `value` above stays the CANONICAL form; every non-underscore key here is a verbatim-correct reading of THIS notice, and comparison is canonical-after-alias -- a written string is mapped to its canonical form FIRST, and only canonical forms are compared. A raw-string compare against `value` is the wrong comparator for a verbatim field, and it is what made the witness supplier score 0/3 with every answer correct: the witness read the logo, the text layer read its own damaged heading, and the comparator called two correct readings a disagreement. The set is CLOSED -- a spelling not listed here is not accounted for, which is what `wrong` reports. Keys here may not also appear in `not`; the scorer raises on an overlap rather than letting one block win.
accepted.TE Connectivity: The heading as the page prints it, and the canonical form.
accepted.TE Connecvity: The text layer's reading, with the 'ti' ligature dropped -- the same damage that classifies this notice as degraded. Under the mfr-verbatim rule this IS the string the source hands an extractor, so it is verbatim-correct and may not be scored as a miss. It is still not the canonical form and must never be written as one.
accepted.TE: The logo wordmark, which renders as 'TE' over 'connectivity'. This is what the vision witness reads off the page image, and it is a correct reading of what it was shown.

not._was: 'TE Connecvity' and 'TE' were carried HERE, as declared distractors, until 2026-10-09. That was wrong on its face for a verbatim field: each is a faithful reading of a real part of the page, so three fires picked three members of one accepted set and the gate called one of them a failure -- a verdict decided by which member came up, not by whether the extraction was right. Ruled: they are ALIASES, not distractors. This block is kept and left otherwise EMPTY rather than deleted, because an mfr distractor remains possible -- a manufacturer named nowhere on the page would be one -- and an empty block records that the question was asked.

not.2024-06-10: The portal's print stamp -- 'Current Date: 10-Jun-2024' in the top-right rule, and '6/10/24, 11:28 AM' in the browser print header. It is the date the PDF was rendered, NOT the date the notice was published. Unpinned fires flipped between the two, which is what this entry exists to adjudicate.

doc_level_ltb_date.source: Page 1, 'Estimated Dates' table, row 'Last Order Date (Obsolete Parts Only):' -> '06-JUN-2024'. ESTABLISHED 2026-09-30 by rendering page 1 of the source PDF at 500 DPI (pypdfium2) and reading the table region directly -- not from a run, and not from the text layer, which for this notice is a known-damaged source. The whole date surface of that table was read at the same time, so the 'not' block below is CLOSED rather than a sample: 'Last Ship Date of Changed Items (Obsolete Parts Only): 07-JUN-2024'; 'First Ship Date of Changed Items' blank; 'Last Date for Mixed Shipments: No Mixed Shipments'; 'Effectivity Date' and 'Date of First Samples' both blank. The only other dates anywhere on the page are 'PCN Date: 07-JUN-24' and the portal print stamp, both already adjudicated under pub_date.

not.2024-06-07: The ADJACENT ROW -- 'Last Ship Date of Changed Items (Obsolete Parts Only)'. A real date on the real page, one row below the right one, and it is also the correct pub_date, so a run returning it has either taken the wrong row of this table or copied the PCN date. The row label is what distinguishes them; the value cannot.
not.2024-06-08: The second witness's reading of the page image. This date appears NOWHERE on the page -- not in this table, not in any other field. It is a digit substitution by the vision model, the standing failure mode for that witness, so agreeing with it would be agreeing with a fabrication. Recorded here because it was carried as a live candidate until the page was read.

accepted._rule: ACCEPTED-VERBATIM SET, following TYC-PCN-24-210412's and TI_PCN_20210316000's. `value` stays the CANONICAL form; every non-underscore key here is a verbatim-correct reading of THIS page, and comparison is canonical-after-alias -- an exact-string alias is a PASS, a folded-only match is reported `misformatted`, so a listed key must be the exact string a correct reading produces. Writing it as `mfr` is an inference from a domain -- the shape the `Renesas` entry rules out on IDT_PDN_OV-19-05 -- and the schema already carries the field where a parent belongs: the 2026-10-24 fire wrote `mfr_parent: null` here, and establishing that field is separate work.

mfr.source: The page footer, printed on every page: 'PCN23-002 Rev.: A M135112 (01/16/12) File: PCN23-002 This document and its contents are the property of Mini-Circuits.' This template prints NO letterhead name, so the footer is the only place the company names itself, and the occurrence sits inside a NarrativeText element carrying the whole sentence -- nothing the standalone-element arm can read.

not.QUESTIONS: the page-1 heading `[Title] QUESTIONS?`, which reduces to a bare word because `?` is in `_NAME_EDGE_PUNCT` and is then accepted by the shape heuristic. On the sibling notice PCN24-029 -- the same Mini-Circuits template -- the text-layer primacy rule wrote exactly this string as the manufacturer on 2026-10-24, displacing a correct model value. It did NOT happen here, and the reason is an accident of page furniture: this page also prints `[Title] ATTACHMENTS:`, so the arm had two shape-accepted survivors and refused on uniqueness. Recorded as data so a template change cannot quietly turn this notice into the other one.
not.ATTACHMENTS: the other page-1 heading, `[Title] ATTACHMENTS:`, bare for the same reason (`:` is in `_NAME_EDGE_PUNCT`). It is the second survivor described above -- the whole of what kept this notice correct before the 5d766c0 narrowing.

_stochastic_loss._why: A RECORD, NOT A RULE. Nothing in pcn_score.py reads this key and nothing should: these nine MPNs are REQUIRED parts and must keep failing the gate when they are missing. It is written down because the loss is STOCHASTIC and would otherwise be rediscovered as a new regression every time it recurs. Measured 2026-10-15 on pin a72a4a26: three fires of ONE gate invocation on ONE image, and fire 2 scored 10 of 19 while fires 1 and 3 scored 19 of 19, so this is not a property of the image and no code change is implicated by its appearance. THE SIGNATURE IS CONTIGUITY, and that is the whole evidential value: the nine lost MPNs are positions 9-17 of the 19 in this list, an unbroken run, with positions 1-8 and 18-19 kept. Nine independent misreads do not land in a contiguous block; a table segment orphaned at a page break does. The `crops_row_short` flag fire 2 raised on this notice (and fires 1 and 3 did not) is consistent with that reading. DO NOT 'FIX' A RED BY MOVING THESE TO expect_absent_mpns: pcn_score.py refuses a part that is both required and ruled out, and the attempt would assert a false fact about the notice -- all 19 are verbatim in the text layer, per `source` above. The separate one-character substitution seen on this same notice (NSR02F30NXT5G -> NSR02E30NXT5G, 10-13 fire 3) is a DIFFERENT defect and must not be folded into this one. tests/test_onsemi_page_break_orphan.py asserts the contiguity and the non-exemption.

TI_PCN_20210316000.pdf._expect_absent_why: THE CUSTOMER-ALIAS RULING, AS DATA RATHER THAN AS PROSE. These are the 11 distinct customer part numbers in the CUSTOMER PART NUMBER column of page 2's 15-row table, transcribed verbatim from the text layer. They are NOT affected parts (see `source` above); they are the customers' own aliases for the devices beside them, and they are now enumerated a SECOND time in `customer_mpns`, which is what they positively ARE rather than what they are not. KEPT, and no longer resting on an accident: until 2026-10-29 nothing in the extractor implemented any ruling here -- `page.find_tables()` returns ZERO tables for page 2 (measured 2026-10-10 on the real PDF, and again 2026-10-29 under both the 'lines' and the 'text' strategy), so the page was simply invisible to it. As of 2026-10-29 the rule is implemented in the extractor: `table_text_layer._is_customer` vetoes a customer column out of the affected role, so were page 2 ever detected, these 11 would be emitted as `customer_mpn` and never as affected parts. This list is therefore no longer the only thing standing between the gate and 11 spurious parts -- but it stays, because it is the enumeration that makes the guard checkable by NAME. A change to table detection, or a vision pass over page 2, would admit all 11 with no rule having changed. Listed here, such a change fails the gate by NAME (`ruled_out` in pcn_score.py) instead of as 11 anonymous spurious strings, and tests/test_ti_pcn_live_miss.py asserts that page 2 can contribute nothing BUT a real device or one of these. The general question -- whether a Customer Part Number column is a parts source -- is CLOSED, ruled 2026-10-29: it is not, for any notice. The objection recorded here previously was that a global rule would take TYC from 26/26 to 16/26, and that is exactly what happened, deliberately: TYC's 10 are not a different reading of the same column, they were the same conflation, and TYC's entry now carries 16 affected parts plus its own `customer_mpns` of 10. The corpus denominator moved 522 -> 512 with it. The two notices no longer use that column to mean two things.
